title: What If Every Tree on Earth Vanished Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if every tree on Earth vanished tomorrow? You would still be able to breathe.
Earth has about three trillion trees. But most of our oxygen came from the oceans, and burning all organic matter on Earth would use up less than one percent of it.
The danger is carbon. Forests remove roughly sixteen billion tonnes of carbon dioxide a year, and that cleanup would stop.
They also cool the planet. Tropical forests have about fifty percent more cooling effect than their carbon storage alone explains.
Trees pump water into the air that falls again as rain, and forests host more than eighty percent of land species.
We would not suffocate. We would lose the rain, the shade, most land wildlife and a big part of our carbon cleanup.

description:
What if every tree on Earth vanished tomorrow?
Oxygen would not run out, but the carbon cleanup, the cooling and the homes for most land species would.
What should we run through next?
